data.title: Separate hook limits for the main thread and subagents
Add --main-max to the hook
data.description: The shared rules draw two lines: a subagent hands off past 40% of its context, and the integrator stops delegating at 25%. The hook has one `--max`. A subagent's PostToolUse payload carries `agent_id` and the main thread's doesn't, so add `--main-max <percent>` for payloads without an `agent_id`, falling back to `--max`. Red first, in `hook/hook_test.go` and `cmd/contextfill/run_test.go`. Afterwards Ben changes `~/.claude/settings.json` to `contextfill hook --max 40 --main-max 25` (the sandbox can't write it).

criteria.label: A payload without agent_id is judged against --main-max when given, else --max.
A payload with agent_id is always judged against --max.
README and contextfill --help document --main-max.

data.title: Investigate OpenCode's session storage
data.description: Answer the four questions in project/2026-10-24-opencode-support.md from real files, not memory: where a session's messages and token counts live, how a shell inside OpenCode names its session, how it names the model and its window, and whether it has subagents and hooks. OpenCode's data is under ~/.local/share/opencode and ~/.config/opencode, which the sandbox blocks; Ben approved reading those paths with the sandbox off, and driving a live session through tmux. Nothing lifted from those files is committed.

data.text:
Findings are in project/2026-10-24-opencode-findings.md, and scripts/opencode-shape.sh re-runs the store survey. In short:
- Storage: a SQLite store, using the session_v2 and session_message tables (the legacy session and message tables are stale since 2026-08).
- Session ID: OPENCODE_SESSION_ID, and the OPENCODE=1 marker.
- Window: limit.context, complete only from the running server's model.list.
- Subagents: child sessions via parent_id.
- Hooks: no shell hooks; the equivalent is a JS plugin on tool.execute.after.
Open decision: read through the local HTTP API (recommended; discovery via ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json, Basic auth as user opencode), or SQLite plus a dependency.

data.title: Add an OpenCode plugin that reports the fill after a commit
data.description: The OpenCode equivalent of the Claude Code PostToolUse hook. A thin JS plugin on "tool.execute.after": on a bash call it hands the call to `contextfill hook` and appends the answer to the tool's output. The commit test, limits and wording stay in Go's `hook` package; the plugin holds no decision. First verify live, in tmux, that appended output reaches the model. Ship as a file in this repo that's copied or symlinked into ~/.config/opencode/plugin/; npm publishing is Ben's call, not yet made. See section 4 of project/2026-10-24-opencode-findings.md.

The plugin makes no decisions: commit detection and limits live in Go.
README covers installing the plugin.

data.note:
Added an opencode package: Service/ServicePath/LoadService, which read ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json or $XDG_STATE_HOME, and Client, a fill.Source over the server's HTTP API with Basic auth as user "opencode".
- Latest pages assistant steps newest-first, 5 at a time, skipping steps with no tokens or a zero input side. A tokens object missing its input or cache counts is an error.
- The window comes from model.list for the session's directory, cached per client; an unknown model gives Window 0.
- Agents are child sessions via session.list?parentID=; an agent counts as Finished when time.idle >= time.updated.
- Errors: ErrNoServer (missing service file, or connection refused), fill.ErrNoSession (the 404 SessionNotFoundError), and a 401 names service.json.
Fixtures are a synthetic httptest server mirroring the real wrapper and paging, including the cursor the real server returns even on the last page.

data.label: The reader is chosen from the environment, and --harness overrides it.
README and contextfill --help cover OpenCode and --harness.

data.note:
The CLI detects the harness, OPENCODE=1 first (OpenCode inherits Claude Code's variables when started from one), and --harness claude|opencode overrides it; hook rejects --harness.
- OpenCode errors: ErrNoServer exits 5 and names `opencode service start`; an unknown session exits 4 and names `opencode session list`; --max against an unknown window exits 4.
- --json gains a harness field, and fill is null when the window is unknown.
- OpenCode session ids are shown whole, because their prefixes are shared.
Verified live inside an OpenCode shell. That found a real-server quirk: a cursor can't be combined with order. It's fixed, the fake server now enforces it, and the fix is recorded in the findings doc. README, --help and the AGENTS.md head are updated.

data.label: A live OpenCode session shows the model the fill after a commit.
The plugin makes no decisions: commit detection and limits live in Go.

data.note: Added opencode/plugin/contextfill.js, a v2 plugin (default export {id, setup}). On ctx.tool.hook("execute.after") it pipes {tool, sessionID, input} to `contextfill hook --harness opencode` and appends any stdout as a text item to result.content; it never blocks. In Go, hook.RespondOpenCode decides everything: tool == "shell", Commits(), and whether the session is a subagent via Client.IsSubagent (parentID); Limits.For now takes a bool. Verified live: a commit inside OpenCode returned the fill line in the tool output and the model quoted it. That required `opencode reload`, because the background server keeps plugins loaded. The findings doc's v1 plugin section is corrected in place. Not installed globally: the classifier denied the symlink into ~/.config/opencode/plugins, so Ben runs it himself.
